strengths: The character remains the same compact figure. Matched before/current images preserve the oversized soft head, short mittens, attached stub feet, unequal paddles and layered wings; unchanged character.js and shared theme poses corroborate the visual continuity.

The updated offer creates a more clearly upward-facing mitten separated from the ruff in the 160px and 240px comparisons, with the face still the primary anchor. It does not achieve clarity by enlarging a hand or changing body proportions.

Thinking now places the free mitten lower and farther from the ruff while retaining the deliberate chin-hand contact. The visual hierarchy distinguishes the active thinking hand from its quiet partner more cleanly.

Grateful lowers the joined hand shape out of the busiest neck band. Worried preserves a diagonal higher/lower relationship, and Focused presents two lower ready hands. The changes are controlled rather than a wholesale redraw.

The current 390px investigation pose is visibly more upright/upward-facing than the baseline lateral head/gaze pose. This better agrees with the question above the character; 320px and night samples show the same composed attention.

The contextual samples return to a front-facing expression before the offering pose, and the sequence sheets retain a stable offering endpoint. The source restricts composition correction to five attention channels and ends it by 2350ms, protecting the authored return and shared identity.

The readable question/body/link hierarchy and both theme relationships remain intact. The 320px transport wraps without horizontal clipping in the supplied proof; the desktop scene retains its side-by-side relationship.
Unchanged universal day-avatar guidance and existing outlined wordmark remain sound. No extra embellishment or anatomy change was introduced to manufacture novelty.

improvementCriteria: Keep the current unchanged anatomy and paint invariants. Any further gesture improvement should first use pose, contact, orientation, timing or application size; do not add fingers, long arms or oversized mittens.

For stronger small-size craft, test whether the inviting silhouette and Grateful/Shy hand relations can become more distinct at 96–128px without losing intentional chin/clasp contact. Retaining the current result and documenting a larger expressive-use size is valid if alternatives regress.

Keep the successful question-directed attention and complete visitor-facing return in both themes across responsive layouts. Validate perceived sequence/rhythm with actual continuous playback before judging an unintended wrist flick or declaring smoothness.
Preserve the prior day/night avatar usage distinction. A higher overall score must not silently discard its unresolved night 48px weakness.

For actual website acceptance, retain the planned native-phone/enlarged-text checks and grounded project context. Unprimed association, emotion comprehension and delayed recall require separate human evidence; labels and explanatory copy cannot stand in for it.

limits: No new source or browser operation by this reviewer; root supplied the screenshots and browser records.
No continuous normal-speed motion was watched. Sequence sheets cannot establish whether the wrist rotation feels like a flick or whether the notice/read/return rhythm works at playback speed.

The portrait composition still requires vertical scrolling and does not show the full character and all controls in the first viewport. This known tradeoff remains acceptable for the local study, not certified optimal for a future landing page.
No native-phone, GPU-performance, spoken-screen-reader or native menu keyboard-commit verification is added by these browser proofs.
No unfamiliar-human comprehension, association, attachment or recall results. My pose interpretations are expert hypotheses; explanatory labels prime the reading.
Avatar/header assets are unchanged and retain their prior strengths and limits. No live GitHub publication/rendering claim.
Numeric equality of themes and anatomy establishes consistency; it does not prove equal perceptual clarity.
